title: 关山月
titleEn: The Moon over the Mountain Pass
author: 李白
intro: A vast moonrise over the Tianshan mountains opens onto centuries of frontier wars — and ends with soldiers gazing homeward while their wives sigh in a tower far away, under the same moon.
analysis: 《关山月》是乐府旧题，多写边塞士兵的离别之苦。前四句写景，气魄非常大：一轮明月从天山升起，在苍茫的云海中穿行；长风吹过几万里，一直吹过玉门关。月亮和风把广阔的西北边疆连在一起。中间四句写历史：汉朝军队曾在白登山被围，吐蕃一直窥视着青海湾；自古以来这些战场上，从没见过有人活着回来。最后四句写人：守边的士兵望着边城，想家想得满脸愁苦；而今夜家中高楼上的妻子，一定也在不停地叹息。从月亮写到战争，又从战争写到两地相思，场面由大到小，感情越来越深。全诗没有直接说反对战争，却让人感到战争带给普通人的痛苦。
analysisEn: “The Moon over the Mountain Pass” was an old yuefu title for songs about soldiers far from home. Li Bai opens with an enormous landscape: the bright moon rises over the Tianshan mountains and sails through a boundless sea of cloud; a long wind blows tens of thousands of miles, all the way through Jade Gate Pass. Moon and wind tie the whole northwestern frontier together in two strokes. The middle four lines turn to history. Han armies were once trapped on the road to Baideng; the Tibetan armies still eye Qinghai Lake. On these ancient battlefields, no one has ever been seen coming home. The last four lines narrow to people: the garrison soldiers look out over the border town, homesick, their faces full of misery; and tonight, in a tall house far away, their wives must be sighing without rest. The camera moves from sky to history to two single hearts, from very large to very small, and the feeling deepens as it goes. The poem never says war is wrong. It simply shows what war costs ordinary people, and lets the moon shine on both sides of the separation.
background: Li Bai (701–762) is traditionally said to have been born in Suyab, in Central Asia, so the western frontier was part of his family story. In his time the Tang fought long wars with the Tibetan Empire around Qinghai Lake.
pronunciation: 几万里 jǐ；度 dù（同“渡”）；窥 kuī；戍客 shù kè；有人还 huán；当此夜 dāng；未应闲 yīng。机器朗读“还”“应”易读错，已在朗读用字中替换同音字。
version: 采用通行文本。异文：“戍客望边邑”《全唐诗》作“戍客望边色”（注“一作邑”），网站用通行的“边邑”。

lines.zh: 明月出天山，苍茫云海间。
lines.rhythm: 明月/出天山，苍茫/云海间
lines.py: míng yuè chū tiān shān, cāng máng yún hǎi jiān
lines.lit: The bright moon comes out over Tianshan, amid a vast, misty sea of clouds.
lines.en: The bright moon climbs out of the Tianshan range into a boundless sea of cloud.

lines.zh: 长风几万里，吹度玉门关。
lines.rhythm: 长风/几万里，吹度/玉门关
lines.py: cháng fēng jǐ wàn lǐ, chuī dù yù mén guān
lines.lit: A long wind of many ten-thousand li blows across Jade Gate Pass.
lines.en: A wind that has travelled ten thousand miles comes sweeping through Jade Gate Pass.

lines.zh: 汉下白登道，胡窥青海湾。
lines.rhythm: 汉下/白登道，胡窥/青海湾
lines.py: hàn xià bái dēng dào, hú kuī qīng hǎi wān
lines.lit: Han troops went down the Baideng road; the northern tribes spy on Qinghai Bay.
lines.en: Once Han armies marched down the road to Baideng; now raiders watch the shores of Qinghai Lake.

lines.zh: 由来征战地，不见有人还。
lines.rhythm: 由来/征战地，不见/有人还
lines.py: yóu lái zhēng zhàn dì, bù jiàn yǒu rén huán
lines.lit: From of old, in these places of war, none has been seen to return.
lines.en: On these battlefields, since time began, no one has ever come home.
lines.tts: 由来征战地，不见有人环。

lines.zh: 戍客望边邑，思归多苦颜。
lines.rhythm: 戍客/望边邑，思归/多苦颜
lines.py: shù kè wàng biān yì, sī guī duō kǔ yán
lines.lit: The garrison men gaze at the border town; longing to go home, many wear bitter faces.
lines.en: The soldiers stare out over the frontier town, faces worn with longing for home.

lines.zh: 高楼当此夜，叹息未应闲。
lines.rhythm: 高楼/当此夜，叹息/未应闲
lines.py: gāo lóu dāng cǐ yè, tàn xī wèi yīng xián
lines.lit: In the high towers on this night, the sighing surely does not stop.
lines.en: And tonight, in a tall house far away, the sighing will not cease.
lines.tts: 高楼当此夜，叹息未英闲。

words.note: 今新疆境内的大山脉，古时也泛指西北的祁连山一带。
现代汉语书面语仍用，如“暮色苍茫”。
现代汉语仍用，如“黄山云海”。
同“渡”。现代汉语“度过”“渡过”。
在今甘肃敦煌西北，古代通往西域的关口。

words.en: Baideng Hill, where the first Han emperor was besieged
words.note: 在今山西大同，汉高祖曾被匈奴围困七天。

words.en: to spy on; to eye greedily

words.note: 即青海湖，唐和吐蕃常在这里交战。
古义：自古以来。今天“由来”多指来历、起源。
戍：守卫边疆，现代汉语“戍边”。
邑：城镇，今天只用在地名或书面语里。
颜：脸色，现代汉语“颜色”“愁眉苦脸”。

words.en: tall house — here, where the wives live
words.note: 诗词中常代指闺中思妇。

imagery.name: 月
imagery.zh: 同一轮明月照着边关的士兵，也照着家中的妻子，是两地相思的纽带。
imagery.en: The same moon shines on the soldiers at the border and the wives at home — the thread joining two places.

imagery.name: 山
imagery.zh: 天山高远，写出边疆的辽阔和离家之远。
imagery.en: The towering Tianshan shows how vast the frontier is and how far the men are from home.

imagery.name: 云
imagery.zh: 苍茫的云海衬托明月，营造出雄浑又寂寞的边塞夜景。
imagery.en: The endless sea of cloud sets off the moon, creating a frontier night both grand and lonely.

imagery.name: 风
imagery.zh: 长风吹度万里，好像把边关和中原连在一起，也带着思念。
imagery.en: A wind blowing ten thousand miles seems to link the frontier with the heartland, carrying longing with it.

imagery.name: 关
imagery.zh: 玉门关是中原和西域的分界，代表士兵回不去的家乡之门。
imagery.en: Jade Gate Pass marks the edge of the homeland — the gate the soldiers cannot pass back through.
